> **Notional system.** KESTREL is fictional. Its control selection uses NIST's published baselines as a stand-in, as Control Set explains.

# KESTREL Security Controls Traceability Matrix (SCTM)

*Generated by `tools/sctm/build.py` from the CCSD, the SADD, and the curated dispositions in `tools/sctm/dispositions.py`. Edit those, not this page.*

This matrix carries every control in KESTREL's approved set to the SADD outcomes that implement it, the providers it inherits from, and where its evidence is kept. The same rows are kept as OSCAL in KESTREL's system security plan, [`kestrel-ssp.oscal.json`](../06-ssp/kestrel-ssp.oscal.json), under SCTM Automation via Machine-Readable Format (OSCAL) (`GV-5.9.4`).

## Control Set

The CCSD selects KESTREL's controls from the CNSSI 1253 columns for High confidentiality, High integrity, and Moderate availability. This notional example does not reproduce those columns. It uses NIST's OSCAL [High baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_HIGH-baseline_profile.json) and [privacy baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/usnistgov/oscal-content/main/nist.gov/SP800-53/rev5/json/NIST_SP-800-53_rev5_PRIVACY-baseline_profile.json) as a stand-in. The CCSD's tailoring actions then apply. SI-8 is removed with its enhancements, and SR-11(3) and SA-9(5) are added.

That gives 423 controls in the set. The cloud, OT, and IL5 overlays would add rows a real selection carries, and this stand-in omits them.

---

## How to Read Each Row

- **Control ID** and **Control Name** come from NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5.
- **Designation** is System-Specific when KESTREL implements the whole control, Inherited when a provider does, and Hybrid when both do.
- **Implementation Status** comes from the project board, through the SSP's status snapshot. A control is Planned until its outcomes' work starts reaching Done, Partially implemented once some has, and Implemented when every claiming outcome is done. A Hybrid control's status is KESTREL's own part, since the provider's part is already in place.
- **Narrative** says how KESTREL meets the control, naming the products and where they run, in future tense until the work is built. It then gives any provider's part and any CCSD tailoring. Its last sentence links to the part of the [SSP](../06-ssp/index.md) that tells the whole story, and each linked entry closes with its [Security Implementation Plan](../04-sip/index.md) record.
- **Evidence** for every row is kept in the program evidence repository under `evidence/<family>/<control>/`, under Compliance Evidence Collection and Retention (`CO-1.3`). Nothing is collected yet.

## Gaps for the SADD's Gap Register

These rows go to the SADD's gap register (Section 9) for disposition.

**Held but unclaimed (22).** An outcome already does this, or is where it belongs, but its mapping does not claim the control. Each needs a claim added to the outcome, or a recorded reason it stays unclaimed.

| Control | Held By | How |
|---|---|---|
| AC-3(14) | CO-4.2 | The privacy officer handles individual access requests. |
| AU-3(1) | DE-2.1 | Logging adds the detail each source class needs. |
| AU-3(3) | DE-2.4 | Application logs limit the personal information they record. |
| AU-5(2) | DE-3.1 | A silent log source alerts within the hour. |
| CM-3(6) | DA-3.13 | Cryptographic changes go through the KMP and the Configuration Control Board. |
| MA-2(2) | DI-2.4 | Maintenance is scheduled and recorded in Jira Service Management. |
| MA-4(3) | ID-4.7 | Vendor sessions run from the vendor host pool, built to KESTREL's baseline. |
| MA-5(1) | DI-2.4 | Uncleared vendor engineers are escorted at all times. |
| MP-6(3) | DI-5.1 | The media intake station scans media before use. |
| PL-9 | NE-1.1 | Policy as code is defined once and deployed everywhere. |
| PT-5 | CO-4.2 | The account request form carries the Privacy Act statement. |
| PT-5(2) | CO-4.2 | The Privacy Act statement is given where data is collected. |
| PT-7 | CO-4.2 | The PIA identifies any special category of personal information. |
| PT-7(2) | CO-1.1 | Intelligence oversight bars collection on First Amendment activity. |
| SA-8(33) | AI-1.2 | Privacy requirements minimize personal data by design. |
| SA-16 | GV-3.2 | A contract clause requiring developer-provided training belongs in the contract security requirements, still to be confirmed. |
| SA-21 | GV-3.2 | A contract clause requiring screening of developers belongs in the contract security requirements, still to be confirmed. |
| SC-7(24) | DA-1.5 | Data loss prevention watches personal information at the boundary. |
| SI-5(1) | RK-2.3 | CSSP advisories arrive automatically as STIX over TAXII. |
| SI-18 | CO-4.2 | The PIA sets how personal data accuracy is maintained. |
| SI-18(4) | CO-4.2 | The privacy officer handles correction requests. |
| SR-9(1) | GV-3.4 | Supplier assessments cover multiple stages of the supply chain, still to be confirmed. |

**No owner (1).** No outcome or provider holds these.

- AC-18(5)

**Narrow owners (2).** These rest only on narrow outcomes. The SCTM does not read them as system-wide, and each still needs a system-wide owner named.

- CM-6(2): DI-4.1, AI-4.18, AI-9.3 (Partial)
- SA-5: AI-5.8, AI-6.2 (Partial)

### CM: Configuration Management

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CM-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the configuration management policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Configuration Management Plan (CMP) will hold the procedures that carry it out. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DI-6.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-61-configuration-management-plan-cmp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| CM-2 | Baseline Configuration | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's baselines will come from DISA STIGs and SRGs, with the Cloud Computing SRG's IL5 requirements in the cloud. They are held as code. Landing zone modules define the cloud's hub and spokes, and Packer images define servers and VDI desktops. Containers start from Iron Bank base images, managed services follow Azure Policy initiatives, and Ansible roles carry the baselines on premises. Fleet equipment follows each manufacturer's hardening guidance, and each release carries a versioned runtime baseline. The SSP describes them under [DI-3.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-31-secure-configurations), [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [DI-3.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-33-secure-storage-baselines), [DI-3.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-34-secure-platform-services-and-application-baselines), [DI-3.5](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-35-secure-otlegacy-device-baselines), [NE-1.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-11-network-centralization-and-standardization), [AP-4.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-44-runtime-security-baseline). |
| CM-2(2) | Baseline Configuration \| Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency | System-Specific | Planned | Baselines will be kept current and accurate by the same automation that applies them. The landing zone modules, Packer images, and Ansible roles live in GitLab. A change to a baseline is therefore a reviewed merge request, and every new build picks it up. Training environments pin their dependencies and image digests, and each run checks its environment against the approved baseline before it starts. System prompts are versioned with each release in the same way. The SSP describes them under [DI-3.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-31-secure-configurations), [AI-3.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-32-experiment-tracking-and-reproducibility), [AI-4.13](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-413-reproducibility-controls), [AI-8.10](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-810-system-prompt-governance). |
| CM-2(3) | Baseline Configuration \| Retention of Previous Configurations | System-Specific | Planned | Previous configurations will be kept so a change can be rolled back. GitLab keeps the full history of every baseline and policy as code. Artifactory keeps every fielded release and the certified release before it, and the model registry keeps each model's prior certified version. Backups keep each system's configuration as part of its tier's backup policy. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.8](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-48-vulnerability-and-patch-management), [AP-5.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-54-registry-hygiene-report), [AI-9.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-97-model-registry-hygiene-report), [RC-1.4](../06-ssp/10-recovery.md#rc-14-otlegacy-configuration-and-engineering-backup). |
| CM-2(7) | Baseline Configuration \| Configure Systems and Components for High-risk Areas | System-Specific | Planned | The privileged access workstations are KESTREL's only endpoints that stay outside the VDI pools, and none of them travels. They are enrolled in Configuration Manager in the Tier 0 enclave and held to a dedicated compliance policy. KESTREL has no mobile devices, so no travel configuration is needed. The SSP describes it under [DI-4.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-41-device-compliance). |
| CM-3 | Configuration Change Control | System-Specific | Planned | Every change will have a change record. For anything defined as code, that is the merged GitLab merge request, approved by a second reviewer. Jira Service Management holds the record for everything else, including fleet changes. System prompts change only through the pipeline, reviewed like code. Changes to the shared firewall rule base, the identity provider, or an interconnection go to the Configuration Control Board, which the chief engineer chairs. Emergency changes run through CyberArk and are reviewed within two business days. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-22-asset-lifecycle-change-control), [NE-1.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-11-network-centralization-and-standardization), [AI-8.10](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-810-system-prompt-governance), [GV-1.5](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-15-configuration-control-board). |
| CM-3(1) | Configuration Change Control \| Automated Documentation, Notification, and Prohibition of Changes | System-Specific | Planned | GitLab will enforce change control automatically. Protected branches block a merge until its required approvals and checks pass. Code owners mark sensitive paths, such as pipeline definitions, infrastructure as code, admission policy, and agent configuration. A change to one needs extra approval and raises an alert in Splunk. Open Policy Agent rejects changes that break policy in the pipeline and at cluster admission. Privileged changes to training configuration alert the ML Team and the Security Team. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.18](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-218-pre-merge-sensitive-repo-file-change-detection), [AP-2.19](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-219-policy-as-code-evaluation), [AI-4.17](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-417-privileged-config-change-alerting). |
| CM-3(2) | Configuration Change Control \| Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes | System-Specific | Planned | Changes will be tested before they reach production. Cloud changes go first to the owning team's stage cluster. Tier 0 and data center changes go to the alternate site's standby or a lab, and a change with neither records an exception and gets extra checking afterward. A compliance scan after the change closes its record. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-22-asset-lifecycle-change-control). |
| CM-3(4) | Configuration Change Control \| Security and Privacy Representatives | System-Specific | Planned | Security sits on the change path itself. A change to a sensitive repository path needs the Platform Team's and the Security Team's approval beyond the team's own reviewer. The PMO ISSE and the ISSM are members of the Configuration Control Board. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.18](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-218-pre-merge-sensitive-repo-file-change-detection), [AI-4.17](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-417-privileged-config-change-alerting). |
| CM-3(6) | Configuration Change Control \| Cryptography Management | System-Specific | Planned | Changes to cryptographic mechanisms, such as algorithms, key lengths, and certificate profiles, will go through the Key Management Plan and the Configuration Control Board. The design meets it, but the SADD does not yet claim it, so it is tracked as a gap. |
| CM-4 | Impact Analyses | System-Specific | Planned | Each change will carry a security impact note, answering what it touches, whether it changes a boundary or an identity's access, and which controls it affects. Every note feeds a Security Impact Analysis, which the ISSM runs against what the authorization was granted on. A significant change goes to the SCA and the AO before it is made. A change to a system prompt's role or limits also triggers jailbreak and injection testing. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-22-asset-lifecycle-change-control), [AI-8.10](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-810-system-prompt-governance), [GV-5.11](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-511-security-impact-analysis-sia). |
| CM-4(1) | Impact Analyses \| Separate Test Environments | System-Specific | Planned | Changes will be analyzed in separate environments before production. Each team has its own dev, test, and stage clusters, with stage carrying production's configuration. On-premises and Tier 0 changes are tried on the alternate site's standby or in a lab. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-22-asset-lifecycle-change-control). |
| CM-4(2) | Impact Analyses \| Verification of Controls | System-Specific | Planned | After a change is made, the controls its impact analysis identified will be checked again. The check confirms each control is implemented correctly, operating as intended, and meeting its requirements. The results are recorded on the Security Impact Analysis record. The SSP describes it under [GV-5.11](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-511-security-impact-analysis-sia). |
| CM-5 | Access Restrictions for Change | System-Specific | Planned | Only approved people and pipelines will be able to change production. Each team's pipeline identity reaches only its own repositories and dev/test spoke. Only the release identity, on a separate protected runner, can deploy to production, and it is unlocked only by Certification to Field's approval. Protected branches require a second reviewer and signed commits, with no administrator bypass. Training identities write only to their own run's output. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.22](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-222-least-privilege-cibuild-infrastructure-access), [AP-4.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-41-branch-protection-policy-report), [AP-4.6](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-46-application-rollback-progressive-delivery-and-feature-flag-governance), [AI-4.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-42-least-privilege-training-infrastructure-access). |
| CM-5(1) | Access Restrictions for Change \| Automated Access Enforcement and Audit Records | System-Specific | Planned | GitLab will enforce those restrictions and record each one. Every review, approval, dismissal, and override streams to Splunk, where Platform Team administrators cannot change it. Each approval is checked against the approver's entitlement in Entra ID Governance at the time it was given. The SSP describes them under [AP-4.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-41-branch-protection-policy-report), [AP-4.6](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-46-application-rollback-progressive-delivery-and-feature-flag-governance). |
| CM-6 | Configuration Settings | System-Specific | Planned | Each class of asset will be configured to its baseline's settings. Domain controllers, certificate authorities, and sync servers follow their DISA STIGs. Containers must run as non-root with a read-only filesystem, dropped capabilities, and resource limits. Fleet equipment follows its manufacturer's hardening guide. Each deviation from a STIG is recorded with its reason and approved through change control. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-14-identity-platform-threat-detection-and-hardening), [ID-1.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-15-directory-and-tier-0-infrastructure-hardening), [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [DI-4.7](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-47-ot-baseline-configuration-drift-detection), [NE-1.2](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-12-network-infrastructure-device-hardening), [AP-2.16](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-216-container-hardening-verification), [AP-3.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-33-application-security-and-development-asd-stig-compliance). |
| CM-6(1) | Configuration Settings \| Automated Management, Application, and Verification | System-Specific | Planned | Settings will be applied and checked automatically. OpenTofu and Ansible apply them, Azure Policy and Conftest check infrastructure as code before it deploys, and Gatekeeper rejects non-compliant workloads at admission. Azure Machine Configuration, Defender for Cloud CSPM, and ACAS STIG audits then check running systems continuously, and results feed compliance dashboards in Splunk. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-21-secure-resource-provisioning), [DI-4.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-41-device-compliance), [DI-4.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-44-compute-configuration-monitoring), [DI-4.5](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-45-storage-configuration-monitoring), [DI-4.6](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-46-platform-services-and-application-configuration-monitoring), [NE-1.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-11-network-centralization-and-standardization), [AP-2.15](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-215-iac-scanning), [AP-2.16](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-216-container-hardening-verification), [AP-3.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-33-application-security-and-development-asd-stig-compliance), [AP-4.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-44-runtime-security-baseline), [AI-4.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-48-training-infrastructure-iac-scanning), [AI-4.18](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-418-hyperparameter-change-alerting). |
| CM-6(2) | Configuration Settings \| Respond to Unauthorized Changes | System-Specific | Planned | When an unauthorized change is found, KESTREL will respond automatically where it can do so safely. A privileged access workstation that drifts loses Tier 0 sign-in until Configuration Manager restores it. A change to a training hyperparameter outside its approved range alerts the ML Team, and a retraining pipeline that fails its integrity check halts. Firewall policy that drifts from its repository is reverted within one business day. A system-wide owner is still to be named, and it is tracked as a gap. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-41-device-compliance), [AI-4.18](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-418-hyperparameter-change-alerting), [AI-9.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-93-retraining-pipeline-integrity-verification). |
| CM-7 | Least Functionality | System-Specific | Planned | Every asset will run only the services its function needs. Images are built minimal, managed services expose only private endpoints, and the CMP lists the ports, protocols, and services each asset type may use. Host firewalls and the shared firewall rule base deny everything else. The SSP describes them under [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [DI-3.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-34-secure-platform-services-and-application-baselines), [DI-4.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-42-policy-service-restrictions), [NE-2.2](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-22-platform-service-network-integration), [NE-2.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-27-secure-remote-access). |
| CM-7(1) | Least Functionality \| Periodic Review | System-Specific | Planned | Running services will be reviewed against the permitted list. ACAS scans and Defender for Cloud CSPM look for services outside the CMP's list. Network flows and firewall rules are reviewed against the approved flow map, and API Management reports any API endpoint that answers but was never registered. The SSP describes them under [DI-4.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-43-unapproved-service-usage-monitoring-and-alerting), [NE-1.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-13-insecure-services-and-protocols), [NE-2.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-26-web-application-firewall), [AP-5.7](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-57-runtime-api-inventory-and-governance). |
| CM-7(2) | Least Functionality \| Prevent Program Execution | System-Specific | Planned | App Control for Business on Windows and fapolicyd on Red Hat Enterprise Linux will block any program that is not on the allow-list. They run in audit mode during Phase 2 and enforce by Phase 3. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| CM-7(5) | Least Functionality \| Authorized Software — Allow-by-exception | System-Specific | Planned | Software will run by exception only. The allow-lists name the programs each class of host may run, and everything else is denied. To add a program, a team asks through Jira Service Management and the Security Team reviews the request. The Platform Team then adds it to the signed policy through a merge request. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| CM-8 | System Component Inventory | System-Specific | Planned | Jira Service Management Assets will be KESTREL's one inventory. Azure Resource Graph feeds it for the cloud, Defender for Endpoint for on-premises hosts, and the Cisco APIC for the data center network. Passive sensors and Fleet Operations' records feed the fleet. Each application and each certified model version is registered too, and so are third-party products once their supplier assessment passes. The SSP describes them under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery), [DI-1.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-12-otlegacy-passive-protocol-aware-discovery), [DI-2.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-23-resource-decommissioning-governance), [AP-4.7](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-47-application-registration-and-inventory-logging), [AI-6.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-67-model-registration-and-inventory-logging), [GV-3.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-31-vendor-security-risk-assessment), [GV-4.6](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-46-aiml-vendormodel-risk-assessment). |
| CM-8(1) | System Component Inventory \| Updates During Installation and Removal | System-Specific | Planned | The inventory will change when components do. Provisioning and decommissioning update it as part of the same change, and a deployment to production fails unless its application is registered. Each certified model version is registered when it is certified. The SSP describes them under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery), [AP-4.7](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-47-application-registration-and-inventory-logging), [AI-6.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-67-model-registration-and-inventory-logging). |
| CM-8(2) | System Component Inventory \| Automated Maintenance | System-Specific | Planned | The inventory will be maintained automatically from the cloud's resource inventory, the endpoint agents, and the SDN controller. A deployment inventory in Splunk compares what is running with what was certified, and the model registry reports its own state each month. The SSP describes them under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery), [AP-5.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-55-deployment-inventory-report), [AI-9.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-97-model-registry-hygiene-report). |
| CM-8(3) | System Component Inventory \| Automated Unauthorized Component Detection | System-Specific | Planned | Unauthorized components will be detected automatically. A subscription created outside the landing zone alerts, and so does a device the Cisco APIC does not recognize. Passive sensors flag unknown devices on the ground segment. Anything running in production that was never certified is flagged, and the model registry admits only models from approved sources. The SSP describes them under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery), [DI-1.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-12-otlegacy-passive-protocol-aware-discovery), [AP-5.5](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-55-deployment-inventory-report), [AI-9.6](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-96-trusted-model-registry-source-validation). |
| CM-8(4) | System Component Inventory \| Accountability Information | System-Specific | Planned | Every asset will carry tags naming its owning team, segment, environment, data classification, mission criticality, and end-of-support date. The pipeline rejects an untagged cloud resource, and Fleet Operations tags fleet equipment when it is received. The SSP describes it under [DI-1.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-13-resource-tagging-and-ownership-strategy). |
| CM-9 | Configuration Management Plan | System-Specific | Planned | The Platform Team will write the Configuration Management Plan, with Fleet Operations writing the OT and legacy sections and IT Operations the maintenance sections. The Security Team reviews it, and the Configuration Control Board approves it. It is revised each year and after any significant change, such as a new spoke or interconnection. The SSP describes it under [DI-6.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-61-configuration-management-plan-cmp). |
| CM-10 | Software Usage Restrictions | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will track the license terms of every licensed product, including the foundation model's terms, in Jira Service Management Assets. Peer-to-peer file sharing software is prohibited. The SSP describes it under [DI-1.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-11-asset-inventory-and-discovery). |
| CM-11 | User-installed Software | System-Specific | Planned | Users will not be able to install software. Allow-listing on every host blocks anything not on the approved list, and new software reaches a host only through the request and merge process described for CM-7(5). The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| CM-12 | Information Location | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will know where its information lives. The Data Team labels every record at ingest, and OpenMetadata catalogs every data store and classifies databases and structured files by their content. The catalog is checked against the CCSD's information types. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.1](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-11-data-discovery-labeling-and-classification). |
| CM-12(1) | Information Location \| Automated Tools to Support Information Location | System-Specific | Planned | OpenMetadata will scan the data stores automatically over a read-only identity, so the record of where information lives stays current without manual surveys. The SSP describes it under [DA-1.1](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-11-data-discovery-labeling-and-classification). |

### IA: Identification and Authentication

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| IA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the identification and authentication policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Account Management Plan (AMP) will hold the procedures that carry it out, covering authenticators, assurance levels, and sessions. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [ID-5.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-51-account-management-plan-amp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| IA-2 | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) | System-Specific | Planned | Every person will be uniquely identified and authenticated before reaching anything in KESTREL. Active Directory in the mission data center will hold each user's account, and Entra ID will authenticate cloud sign-in against a synchronized copy of it. Group or shared accounts will not be used for everyday access. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.3](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-13-centralized-identity-platform). |
| IA-2(1) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Multi-factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts | System-Specific | Planned | Privileged accounts will authenticate with a CAC, which combines the card with its PIN. Administrators will sign in with the card first, through Entra certificate-based authentication or Active Directory smart card logon. Only then does CyberArk or Entra Privileged Identity Management grant a privileged role. The directory and station break-glass accounts are the one exception. They use console-only passwords under a compensating control, held by two custodians and changed after every use. CCSD tailoring action 6 (compensating control) applies, pending the AO's approval. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(2) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Multi-factor Authentication to Non-privileged Accounts | System-Specific | Planned | Non-privileged accounts will authenticate with a smart card as well, in every location. DoD users and performers will use their CAC, vendors an ECA credential, and partners a certificate from their own nation's PKI. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(5) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Individual Authentication with Group Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Built-in administrative accounts on appliances, hypervisors, and the HSMs will be reachable only through CyberArk. An administrator must first authenticate to CyberArk as an individual with a CAC. CyberArk then injects the shared credential into a recorded session, so the administrator never sees it and every use is tied to a person. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-44-privileged-credential-vaulting-and-session-brokering). |
| IA-2(8) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Access to Accounts — Replay Resistant | System-Specific | Planned | Certificate-based authentication will be used for every network sign-in, and it resists replay because each logon proves possession of the card's private key against a fresh challenge. The break-glass passwords are the only authenticators that would not resist replay. They are limited to named local consoles and never cross a network. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-2(12) | Identification and Authentication (Organizational Users) \| Acceptance of PIV Credentials | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will accept DoD CACs as PIV credentials. Entra certificate-based authentication will accept them in the cloud, and Active Directory smart card logon on premises. Each card's certificate is validated against DoD PKI and checked for revocation. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-3 | Device Identification and Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Devices will be authenticated before they connect. In the data center and at the alternate site, Cisco ISE will require 802.1X with EAP-TLS on every wired port, using device certificates from the program PKI. The operating sites follow in Phase 3. Each aircraft and ground control station will authenticate on the datalinks with its own program PKI device identity. Equipment that cannot hold a certificate will be admitted by its registered hardware address, and only to its own zone. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-37-otlegacy-device-identity-controls), [NE-1.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-17-network-access-control-nac8021x). |
| IA-4 | Identifier Management | System-Specific | Planned | Each person's identifier will be assigned at enrollment and bound to their CAC record, or to their sponsor's record for partners and vendors. IT Operations will assign identifiers through Jira Service Management and Entra ID Governance. Each new account will be checked against existing ones, so no person holds two identities and no identifier is assigned to a second person. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment), [ID-1.8](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-18-account-lifecycle-and-identity-data-quality). |
| IA-4(4) | Identifier Management \| Identify User Status | System-Specific | Planned | Each identifier will show the user's status. CAC affiliation will mark contractors, and a nationality attribute will mark partners and other foreign nationals. Roles and access policies can then tell these populations apart. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-5 | Authenticator Management | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will manage every authenticator it uses through a defined lifecycle. DoD issues and revokes the CACs. The program PKI will issue, renew, and revoke device and workload certificates, with its keys in the nShield HSMs and its certificates tracked in Keyfactor Command. Windows LAPS and group Managed Service Accounts will rotate local administrator and service passwords. Vendor-default credentials will be replaced before any server controller or fleet device is fielded. After a confirmed compromise, every affected authenticator will be reset. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-15-directory-and-tier-0-infrastructure-hardening), [ID-2.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-22-credential-management), [ID-3.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-37-otlegacy-device-identity-controls), [DI-3.2](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-32-secure-compute-baselines), [RS-3.4](../06-ssp/09-response.md#rs-34-eradication-and-threat-removal). |
| IA-5(1) | Authenticator Management \| Password-based Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Passwords will remain only on the break-glass accounts. Each password will be split between two custodians, sealed, and changed after every use. The AMP will set its length and composition. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-5(2) | Authenticator Management \| Public Key-based Authentication | Hybrid | Planned | Certificate validation will build a path to an approved trust anchor and check revocation at each session. DoD PKI, the External Certificate Authorities, and approved partner PKIs supply the anchors. Services will accept a cached revocation response for up to 24 hours, and the ground control stations will check a local list refreshed daily and before each flight. Private keys stay on the CAC or in the HSMs, and service accounts will authenticate with certificates wherever they can. **Inherited from DoD PKI:** The DoD and External Certificate Authority trust anchors. The SSP describes them under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship), [ID-2.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-22-credential-management), [ID-3.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-32-application-and-service-account-identities). |
| IA-5(6) | Authenticator Management \| Protection of Authenticators | System-Specific | Planned | Authenticators will be kept out of code, images, and settings. Each cloud spoke's Key Vault will hold that spoke's secrets, and CyberArk will vault administrative credentials and inject them only into recorded sessions. Pipeline and training jobs will receive short-lived tokens through workload identity rather than stored credentials. The foundation model is reached by workload identity with key-based access disabled, so no API key exists to protect. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-36-secrets-and-credentials-protection), [ID-4.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-44-privileged-credential-vaulting-and-session-brokering), [AP-2.25](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-225-ci-credential-and-secrets-management), [AI-4.19](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-419-training-credential-secrets-management), [AI-8.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-83-third-partyfoundation-model-api-dependency-governance). |
| IA-6 | Authentication Feedback | System-Specific | Planned | Sign-in pages and consoles will hide what a user types and will not say which part of a failed logon was wrong. Failed attempts will be limited as the AMP sets. A ground control station whose aircraft is airborne will delay the next prompt and alert instead of locking the account. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-21-user-authentication-controls). |
| IA-7 | Cryptographic Module Authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Operators of the nShield HSMs will authenticate with smart cards from the HSMs' own card sets, and sensitive key operations will need a quorum of those cards. Software cryptographic modules will authenticate their callers through the identity platform. The SSP describes it under [DA-3.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-34-hsm-and-hardware-root-of-trust-management). |
| IA-8 | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) | System-Specific | Planned | People outside the organization will be identified and authenticated before reaching their part of KESTREL. Vendor support engineers will sign in with ECA Medium Hardware credentials through Entra certificate-based authentication. Partner systems will authenticate to the partner API with mutual TLS, using certificates from their own nation's PKI or an ECA. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(1) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Acceptance of PIV Credentials from Other Agencies | System-Specific | Planned | PIV credentials issued by other federal agencies will be accepted through the same certificate-based authentication, provided their issuers are on KESTREL's trust list. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(2) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Acceptance of External Authenticators | System-Specific | Planned | Only external authenticators from issuers on KESTREL's trust list will be accepted. The list names the External Certificate Authorities and each partner nation's issuing authorities, and adding a partner nation requires a CCSD revision. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-8(4) | Identification and Authentication (Non-organizational Users) \| Use of Defined Profiles | System-Specific | Planned | Partner connections will follow defined profiles. Partner systems will use X.509 certificates over mutual TLS. Partner identity providers, when they join in Phase 3, will federate using SAML or OIDC profiles agreed with each partner. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-12-external-pki-trust-and-sponsorship). |
| IA-11 | Re-authentication | System-Specific | Planned | Users will be asked to authenticate again when risk or context changes. Administrative consoles will always require fresh authentication, and activating a privileged role will too. Cloud and VDI sessions will end and require sign-in again when the AMP's session limits are reached, or sooner if continuous access evaluation finds the risk severe. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-26-continuous-authentication). |
| IA-12 | Identity Proofing | System-Specific | Planned | Every person will be proofed before KESTREL issues an account, at the assurance level the AMP sets for their population. DoD users and performers are proofed through their CAC issuance, and KESTREL binds each account to that record. Partners and vendors will be proofed through a KESTREL sponsor's attestation. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(2) | Identity Proofing \| Identity Evidence | System-Specific | Planned | The evidence behind each enrollment will be recorded in Jira Service Management. For DoD users and performers, that is the CAC record. For partners and vendors, it is the sponsor's attestation and the documents it relies on. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(3) | Identity Proofing \| Identity Evidence Validation and Verification | System-Specific | Planned | IT Operations will validate the evidence at enrollment. Each CAC will be checked against DoD PKI, and each sponsor's attestation against that sponsor's agreement with KESTREL. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |
| IA-12(4) | Identity Proofing \| In-person Validation and Verification | Inherited | Inherited | DoD validates each person's identity evidence in person when it issues their CAC. KESTREL relies on that step and does not repeat it. |
| IA-12(5) | Identity Proofing \| Address Confirmation | System-Specific | Planned | For DoD users and performers, CAC issuance confirms the address of record. For partners and vendors, a registration code or notice of proofing will be sent out of band to the address their sponsor records. The SSP describes it under [ID-1.1](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-11-identity-proofing-and-enrollment). |

### MA: Maintenance

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the maintenance policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Configuration Management Plan's maintenance section, written by IT Operations, will hold the procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| MA-2 | Controlled Maintenance | Hybrid | Planned | On-premises hardware maintenance will be scheduled in Jira Service Management, escorted, and recorded. The owning team's lead approves it, and Tier 0 maintenance also needs the Platform Team lead. Failed drives stay on site for sanitization. From Phase 3, fleet maintenance runs only in each operating site's weekly window, never while an aircraft under its stations is airborne. After maintenance, a compliance scan confirms the component still meets its baseline. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Maintenance of the cloud hardware. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access), [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-2(2) | Controlled Maintenance \| Automated Maintenance Activities | System-Specific | Planned | Maintenance will be scheduled, tracked, and recorded in Jira Service Management, so each maintenance action and its change share one record. The design meets it, but the SADD does not yet claim it, so it is tracked as a gap. |
| MA-3 | Maintenance Tools | System-Specific | Planned | The Security Team will approve the diagnostic tools that maintenance may use. Each tool is scanned at the media intake station before use. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-3(1) | Maintenance Tools \| Inspect Tools | System-Specific | Planned | Maintenance tools will be inspected before use, both those KESTREL holds and those a vendor brings, to confirm they are approved and unmodified. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access), [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-3(2) | Maintenance Tools \| Inspect Media | System-Specific | Planned | Media carrying diagnostic or test programs will be scanned for malicious code at the media intake station before it is used on any KESTREL system. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access), [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-3(3) | Maintenance Tools \| Prevent Unauthorized Removal | System-Specific | Planned | Maintenance equipment will not leave with KESTREL information on it. Failed drives stay on site, and any other component leaving the facility first has its storage sanitized with Blancco, or removed and kept. HSMs are zeroized before they ship. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |
| MA-4 | Nonlocal Maintenance | Hybrid | Planned | Vendor engineers will perform remote maintenance only from the dedicated vendor host pool in Azure Virtual Desktop. They sign in with ECA Medium Hardware credentials, and only for an open Jira Service Management case. CyberArk brokers and records each session, which lasts at most eight hours and ends when the case closes. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Nonlocal maintenance of the cloud hardware. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.7](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-47-access-process-for-third-party-support). |
| MA-4(3) | Nonlocal Maintenance \| Comparable Security and Sanitization | System-Specific | Planned | Remote maintenance will run from systems KESTREL controls. Vendor sessions start in the vendor host pool, which is built to KESTREL's own VDI baseline, rather than from the vendor's device. The design meets it, but the SADD does not yet claim it, so it is tracked as a gap. |
| MA-5 | Maintenance Personnel | Hybrid | Planned | Only authorized people will perform maintenance. KESTREL's own staff do most of it. A vendor engineer working on site is escorted at all times, and one working remotely is limited to the brokered session for their case. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Maintenance personnel for the cloud hardware. The SSP describes it under [ID-4.5](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-45-otlegacy-scheduled-maintenance-window-access). |
| MA-5(1) | Maintenance Personnel \| Individuals Without Appropriate Access | System-Specific | Planned | Vendor engineers without KESTREL access will be escorted on site at all times by an authorized KESTREL staff member. They work only on the equipment in their case. The design meets it, but the SADD does not yet claim it, so it is tracked as a gap. |
| MA-6 | Timely Maintenance | Hybrid | Planned | Support agreements will set replacement times for the HSMs, identity servers, and hub firewalls. Spares cover the mission's tolerance for downtime, including spare stations and aircraft for the fleet. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Timely maintenance of the cloud hardware. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.4](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-24-controlled-maintenance-and-support). |

### SA: System and Services Acquisition

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SA-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the acquisition policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Supply Chain Risk Management Plan will hold the acquisition procedures, including the contract security requirements. The Configuration Control Board will approve both, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework), [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-2 | Allocation of Resources | System-Specific | Planned | Security will be planned and funded as part of each capability. The PMO ISSE turns the CCSD's controls into requirements that enter each team's backlog. The program managers hold a dedicated application security budget line, which funds closing the gaps the PMO ISSE finds. The SSP describes them under [AP-1.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-11-capability-gap-identification-and-planning), [AP-1.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-13-security-requirements-definition). |
| SA-3 | System Development Life Cycle | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will manage development through one lifecycle with security built into each stage. Every application, AI use case, and COTS product enters through intake, is threat-modeled before it is built, and is tested and certified before it is fielded. Roles for each stage are set in the ASP and the AISP. The SSP describes them under [AP-1.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-11-capability-gap-identification-and-planning), [AP-1.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-12-application-intake-and-onboarding), [AI-1.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-11-ai-use-case-intake-and-onboarding). |
| SA-4 | Acquisition Process | System-Specific | Planned | Each acquisition will state the security functions the product must provide, the evidence the supplier must deliver, and the supplier's configuration and supply chain duties. The PMO ISSE writes these requirements from the SADD, and the supply chain lead draws the contract terms from the clause library the SCRM plan sets out. Model selection records the security criteria each model and publisher was assessed against. The SSP describes them under [AP-1.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-13-security-requirements-definition), [AI-1.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-13-model-selection-and-justification), [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(1) | Acquisition Process \| Functional Properties of Controls | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to describe the functional properties of the security controls their products provide, as a clause in the Supply Chain Risk Management Plan's clause library. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(2) | Acquisition Process \| Design and Implementation Information for Controls | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to provide design and implementation information for the security controls in their products, as a clause in the clause library. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(5) | Acquisition Process \| System, Component, and Service Configurations | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to deliver their products in a secure configuration, with that configuration documented, as a clause in the clause library. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(9) | Acquisition Process \| Functions, Ports, Protocols, and Services in Use | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services their products use. That information feeds KESTREL's PPSM registration and the CMP's list of permitted services. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-4(10) | Acquisition Process \| Use of Approved PIV Products | System-Specific | Planned | Products that handle PIV credentials, such as CAC readers and the identity platform, will be bought only from the products approved for FIPS 201 use. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-5 | System Documentation | System-Specific | Planned | Documentation for each certified model will be generated from its validation results. The pipeline produces a model card stating the model's intended use, tested limits, known failure modes, and retraining envelope. The PMO ISSE checks it against its evidence before certification. Administrator and user documentation for other components comes from their suppliers under their contracts. A system-wide owner is still to be named, and it is tracked as a gap. The SSP describes them under [AI-5.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-58-model-card-generation), [AI-6.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-62-model-card-review). |
| SA-8 | Security and Privacy Engineering Principles | System-Specific | Planned | Security engineering principles will be applied as requirements are derived. The PMO ISSE turns the SADD's design principles, such as least privilege, deny by default, and separation of the payload vendor data, into testable requirements for each application. The SSP describes it under [AP-1.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-13-security-requirements-definition). |
| SA-8(33) | Security and Privacy Engineering Principles \| Minimization | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will collect and keep only the personal information its mission needs. Incidental imagery of people is the only personal information in the collection, and training sets keep it only where a detection task requires it. The DMP sets the minimization rules, and the AISP sets the privacy requirements for models. The design meets it, but the SADD does not yet claim it, so it is tracked as a gap. |
| SA-9 | External System Services | System-Specific | Planned | External services will be held to security requirements through their contracts and authorizations. Azure Government is relied on through its IL5 authorization, which the inherited control check confirms each year. The foundation model runs as a deployment inside KESTREL's own tenant, reached only by private endpoint. Applications call no external service outside the boundary except Purview Information Protection in the Microsoft 365 DoD tenant. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.3](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-33-ai-agent-identities), [AP-2.9](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-29-external-runtime-service-and-client-side-code-governance), [AI-8.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-83-third-partyfoundation-model-api-dependency-governance), [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements), [GV-5.12](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-512-inherited-control-validation). |
| SA-9(2) | External System Services \| Identification of Functions, Ports, Protocols, and Services | System-Specific | Planned | Each external service will identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services it uses, as a clause in the clause library. KESTREL registers each one in the DoD PPSM registry. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-9(5) | External System Services \| Processing, Storage, and Service Location | System-Specific | Planned | Processing and storage will stay in United States regions inside the cloud provider's IL5 authorization. CCSD tailoring action 5 records that location as a parameter, covering the foundation model service and KESTREL's Microsoft 365 DoD tenant. CCSD tailoring action 5 (added) applies. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.9](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-29-external-runtime-service-and-client-side-code-governance), [AI-8.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-83-third-partyfoundation-model-api-dependency-governance). |
| SA-10 | Developer Configuration Management | System-Specific | Planned | Changes to the pipeline itself will be controlled. Every team's pipeline extends the Platform Team's templates, and an unapproved change to a pipeline definition stops the run and alerts the Platform Team and the Security Team. From Phase 2, the templates are signed and verified before each job. Training code and its configuration are versioned and reviewed the same way. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.23](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-223-signedverified-pipeline-definitions), [AI-4.12](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-412-signedverified-training-pipeline-definitions). |
| SA-11 | Developer Testing and Evaluation | System-Specific | Planned | Every application and model will be tested before it is fielded. GitLab DAST scans each candidate application build in stage with a test account for each role. Models are tested for jailbreaks, prompt injection, adversarial evasion, data poisoning, and out-of-distribution inputs, against thresholds the AISP sets for each assurance level. The SSP describes them under [AP-3.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-32-dast), [AI-5.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-51-jailbreak-testing), [AI-5.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-52-prompt-injection-testing), [AI-5.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-53-adversarial-evasion-robustness-testing), [AI-5.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-54-data-poisoning-testing), [AI-5.5](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-55-out-of-distribution-robustness-testing). |
| SA-15 | Development Process, Standards, and Tools | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will set its development processes, standards, and tools in the ASP and the AISP. These cover the threat modeling method, the secure coding standard, the policy-as-code gates, the approved component catalogs, and the model optimization techniques. Both plans are reviewed as a whole each year. The SSP describes them under [AP-1.4](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-14-application-threat-modeling), [AP-2.2](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-22-secure-coding-standards-and-build-hardening), [AP-2.19](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-219-policy-as-code-evaluation), [AP-6.1](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-61-application-security-plan-asp), [AI-1.4](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-14-approved-ai-component-catalog), [AI-1.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-17-ai-threat-modeling), [AI-3.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-32-experiment-tracking-and-reproducibility), [AI-6.8](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-68-model-optimization-governance), [AI-10.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-101-aiml-security-plan-aisp). |
| SA-15(3) | Development Process, Standards, and Tools \| Criticality Analysis | System-Specific | Planned | A criticality analysis will identify the components and suppliers KESTREL's essential functions depend on. The supply chain lead maps those dependencies each year, flagging single sources and concentrations, and the contract terms for each supplier follow from that analysis. The SSP describes it under [GV-3.2](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-32-contract-security-requirements). |
| SA-16 | Developer-provided Training | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers of critical components to provide training on their security functions, as a clause in the clause library. The design meets it, but the SADD does not yet claim it, so it is tracked as a gap. |
| SA-17 | Developer Security and Privacy Architecture and Design | System-Specific | Planned | Each application's security architecture will follow the SADD's design, and its threat model will document how the application meets it. The PMO ISSE checks both at the design gate before building starts. The SSP describes it under [AP-1.3](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-13-security-requirements-definition). |
| SA-21 | Developer Screening | System-Specific | Planned | Contracts will require suppliers to screen the developers who work on KESTREL's components, as a clause in the clause library. The design meets it, but the SADD does not yet claim it, so it is tracked as a gap. |
| SA-22 | Unsupported System Components | System-Specific | Planned | Each asset's end of support will be forecast at least 12 months ahead, so it can be replaced in time. An asset kept past its end of support needs an exception, with its compensating controls and a replacement date. The payload processing workstation is the known case, replaced by 2027-09-30, and it connects only if the AO re-dates CCSD tailoring action 3. The SSP describes it under [DI-2.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-23-resource-decommissioning-governance). |

### SC: System and Communications Protection

| Control ID | Control Name | Designation | Implementation Status | Narrative |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SC-1 | Policy and Procedures | System-Specific | Planned | The program manager will issue the system and communications protection policy as part of KESTREL's system security policy. The Key Management Plan will hold the cryptographic procedures, and the CMP the network and boundary procedures. The Configuration Control Board will approve them, and each will be reviewed at least once a year. The SSP describes them under [DA-3.13](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-313-key-management-plan-kmp), [GV-1.1](../06-ssp/11-governance.md#gv-11-security-policy-framework). |
| SC-2 | Separation of System and User Functionality | System-Specific | Planned | Administration will be kept apart from user functions. Tier 0 is administered only from physical privileged access workstations, and Tier 1 from the Platform Team's own Azure Virtual Desktop host pool, never from a user desktop. Administrators hold separate accounts for administrative work. The VDI brokers have their own listener and subnet, apart from user-facing applications. The SSP describes them under [ID-4.2](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-42-privileged-access-workstations-and-administrative-tiering), [NE-2.13](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-213-authorized-cloud-access-point-integration). |
| SC-3 | Security Function Isolation | System-Specific | Planned | Virtualization-based security will isolate the EDR agent and the credential stores on every workstation, desktop, and Windows server. Tamper protection, owned by the Tier 0 administrators and changed only with the Security Team's approval, keeps the EDR agent itself from being switched off. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.3](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-53-host-hardening-and-integrity-protection). |
| SC-4 | Information in Shared System Resources | Hybrid | Planned | Information will not carry over between users of shared resources. Each training run gets its own containers, and its scratch storage is destroyed when it ends, so cached data and tensors cannot reach the next job. Pipeline jobs run on fresh runner pods that are destroyed afterward. **Inherited from Azure Government:** Isolation of shared hardware through the isolated VM sizes IL5 requires. The SSP describes it under [AI-4.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-41-ephemeral-containerized-training-environments). |
| SC-5 | Denial-of-service Protection | Hybrid | Planned | Network-layer floods will be absorbed upstream by DISA's internet access points and the Boundary Cloud Access Point, since the DMZ holds no cloud public addresses. Application Gateway limits the request rate to each user-facing application, and API Management limits each partner and each caller of the model endpoints. DoS protection policies on the cloud hub limit what any one spoke can send. Flood alerts go to Splunk. **Inherited from DISA:** Network-layer flood absorption at the internet access points and the Boundary Cloud Access Point. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.5](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-25-ddos-protection), [NE-2.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-26-web-application-firewall), [AI-8.2](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-82-api-abuse-protection). |
| SC-7 | Boundary Protection | Hybrid | Planned | KESTREL's external boundary will be the Boundary Cloud Access Point and the cloud hub, with the data center hub as the managed interface for its own external links. Internal boundaries divide the cloud's ten spokes, the data center's SDN segments, and the ground segment's IEC 62443 zones. Each ground segment zone joins the IT network only through its conduit. Platform services add their own resource firewalls, admitting only their spoke's private endpoint. **Inherited from DISA:** Boundary protection at the Boundary Cloud Access Point. The SSP describes them under [NE-1.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-14-network-macro-segmentation), [NE-1.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-16-itot-zone-and-conduit-segmentation-iec-62443), [NE-2.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-23-service-native-firewall-configurations). |
| SC-7(3) | Boundary Protection \| Access Points | System-Specific | Planned | External connections will be limited to a small set of managed access points. All user traffic arrives through the Boundary Cloud Access Point and the cloud hub. Outbound traffic leaves only through the hubs, and only for an allow-list of named classes. These are package sources, PKI revocation, the time reference, the threat feed, the Microsoft 365 DoD tenant, and the paging service. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-24-network-firewall). |
| SC-7(4) | Boundary Protection \| External Telecommunications Services | Hybrid | Planned | Each external telecommunications service will have a managed interface. The three dedicated circuits ride DISN through the Boundary Cloud Access Point and terminate on the cloud hub and each site's firewall. Their traffic runs inside IPsec tunnels between the firewalls. BGP sessions are authenticated, and prefix filters accept only KESTREL's address ranges. Every port, protocol, and service crossing them is registered in the DoD PPSM registry with its justification. **Inherited from DISA:** Managed external telecommunications through the Boundary Cloud Access Point. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.1](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-21-private-connectivity), [NE-2.13](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-213-authorized-cloud-access-point-integration). |
| SC-7(5) | Boundary Protection \| Deny by Default — Allow by Exception | System-Specific | Planned | Every boundary will deny traffic by default and allow it by exception. Workload security groups, ACI contracts, Cilium network policies, and the ground segment conduits each allow only mapped flows. Training compute reaches only the model registry, the package mirror, and the training data zone. The SSP describes them under [NE-1.5](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-15-network-micro-segmentation), [NE-1.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-16-itot-zone-and-conduit-segmentation-iec-62443), [AP-2.17](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-217-network-policy-verification), [AI-4.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-43-training-cluster-network-segmentation-and-egress-control). |
| SC-7(7) | Boundary Protection \| Split Tunneling for Remote Devices | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL offers no network tunnel to any remote user. Remote access runs through Pomerium or Azure Virtual Desktop, and neither routes the user's device onto KESTREL's network, so split tunneling cannot occur. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-27-secure-remote-access). |
| SC-7(8) | Boundary Protection \| Route Traffic to Authenticated Proxy Servers | System-Specific | Planned | Outbound traffic will pass through the hubs' firewalls, which decrypt and inspect TLS and apply URL filtering. Remote users reach applications only through Pomerium, the identity-aware proxy, or the VDI brokers, both of which authenticate the user first. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-24-network-firewall), [NE-2.13](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-213-authorized-cloud-access-point-integration). |
| SC-7(18) | Boundary Protection \| Fail Secure | System-Specific | Planned | Boundary devices will fail to a safe state. The firewalls, the access proxy, the VDI brokers, and the cross domain transfer gateway fail closed. On the ground segment, a deep packet inspection fault falls back to a fixed allow-list of each station's approved commands. Launch and recovery keep working, and nothing new is allowed. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.11](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-211-industrial-protocol-filtering-dpi). |
| SC-7(21) | Boundary Protection \| Isolation of System Components | System-Specific | Planned | The components with the most risk will each sit in their own segment. The DMZ, the VDI spoke, and Tier 0 are isolated, and so is each ground segment zone. Each Key Vault is reachable only through its own spoke's private endpoint. The SSP describes them under [NE-1.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-14-network-macro-segmentation), [NE-1.6](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-16-itot-zone-and-conduit-segmentation-iec-62443), [DA-3.11](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-311-secrets-vault-network-security-hardening). |
| SC-7(24) | Boundary Protection \| Personally Identifiable Information | System-Specific | Planned | Data loss prevention will watch personal information at the boundary. The partner API and the cross domain transfer gateway check every release against its markings, and the DMP's rules block personal information on each named outbound path. The design meets it, but the SADD does not yet claim it, so it is tracked as a gap. |
| SC-8 | Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity | System-Specific | Planned | Data in transit will be protected for confidentiality and integrity. Every connection uses TLS 1.2 or later, and services authenticate each other with mutual TLS using program PKI certificates. Traffic across the dedicated circuits runs inside IPsec tunnels. The aircraft datalinks use authenticated encryption on FIPS 140-3 validated crypto modules. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.8](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-28-telemetry-tracking-and-command-ttc-link-security), [DA-2.2](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-22-tls-encryption-enforcement), [DA-2.3](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-23-secure-file-transfer-and-management-protocols). |
| SC-8(1) | Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity \| Cryptographic Protection | System-Specific | Planned | The protection in transit will be cryptographic, using FIPS 140-3 validated modules and CNSA algorithms. The IPsec tunnels run in FIPS-CC mode, and the datalinks use CNSA algorithms under CNSSP 15. The SSP describes them under [NE-2.8](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-28-telemetry-tracking-and-command-ttc-link-security), [DA-2.2](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-22-tls-encryption-enforcement), [DA-2.3](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-23-secure-file-transfer-and-management-protocols). |
| SC-10 | Network Disconnect | System-Specific | Planned | Remote sessions will end after 15 idle minutes, and the Security Team can end any session at once. Cloud and VDI sessions also follow the AMP's limits under continuous access evaluation. The SSP describes it under [NE-2.7](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-27-secure-remote-access). |
| SC-12 | Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management | System-Specific | Planned | Keys will be generated, stored, and managed under the Key Management Plan. The root keys sit in the nShield HSMs in the data center, under KESTREL's own security world. Each spoke's customer-managed keys are generated in the HSMs and imported into Azure Key Vault Premium, which holds them at FIPS 140-3 Level 3. Key Vault rotates its keys on the KMP's schedule, and imported keys are replaced by an HSM job before they expire. Key administration is separated from key use. The SSP describes them under [DA-2.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-25-encryption-key-ownership-and-control), [DA-3.3](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-33-key-management-policies-and-infrastructure), [DA-3.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-35-key-lifecycle-automation). |
| SC-12(1) | Cryptographic Key Establishment and Management \| Availability | System-Specific | Planned | Keys whose loss would destroy data will stay available. Backup set keys and other such keys are escrowed in the alternate site's HSM under split knowledge. Recovering one needs two of the four administrator cards. The SSP describes it under [DA-3.5](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-35-key-lifecycle-automation). |
| SC-13 | Cryptographic Protection | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL will use only FIPS 140-3 validated cryptographic modules and CNSA algorithms. AES-256 protects data at rest. The datalink crypto modules and the HSMs are validated, and so is the cloud's Key Vault Premium. The SSP describes it under [DA-3.1](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-31-fips-140--approved-cryptographic-module-baseline). |
| SC-15 | Collaborative Computing Devices and Applications | System-Specific | Planned | Cameras and microphones will be disabled on the privileged access workstations and in the VDI image, so no collaborative device can be switched on remotely. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| SC-17 | Public Key Infrastructure Certificates | Hybrid | Planned | Certificates will come from approved authorities. The program PKI issues device, workload, and service certificates from issuing authorities under an offline root whose key is held in the HSMs. Keyfactor Command tracks every certificate. User-facing edge services present DoD PKI server certificates that browsers and partner systems already trust. **Inherited from DoD PKI:** DoD PKI server certificates for user-facing edge services. The SSP describes them under [ID-3.4](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-34-server-and-services-authentication), [DA-3.7](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-37-certificate-policies-and-integration), [DA-3.9](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-39-certificate-lifecycle-and-revocation). |
| SC-18 | Mobile Code | System-Specific | Planned | Allow-listing will block unapproved code, including scripts, on every workstation, desktop, and server. Attack surface reduction rules on Windows hosts block scripts and macros from untrusted sources. The SSP describes it under [DI-5.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-51-execution-and-device-control). |
| SC-20 | Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Authoritative Source) | System-Specific | Planned | KESTREL's public names will sit under the program's DoD parent zone, signed with DNSSEC. DoD publishes their delegation records, and the names point only at the access point's published addresses. The SSP describes it under [NE-3.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-33-trusted-dns-service). |
| SC-21 | Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver) | System-Specific | Planned | Every KESTREL resolver will validate DNSSEC on the answers it returns. Hosts may use no other resolver, and the hubs block outbound DNS to anywhere else. The SSP describes it under [NE-3.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-33-trusted-dns-service). |
| SC-22 | Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service | System-Specific | Planned | Name resolution will be redundant and split by role. Infoblox appliances serve the data center and the alternate site, and virtual appliances serve the cloud from Platform Prod. Each operating site has its own resolver pair. No KESTREL resolver answers for the public names, so the authoritative and recursive roles stay separate. The SSP describes them under [NE-3.3](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-33-trusted-dns-service), [NE-3.4](../06-ssp/04-network-and-environment.md#ne-34-private-dns-service). |
| SC-23 | Session Authenticity | System-Specific | Planned | Session authenticity will be protected by TLS on every session and by short-lived, signed tokens. Continuous access evaluation revokes a session's tokens when the account is disabled or its risk becomes severe. The SSP describes it under [ID-2.6](../06-ssp/02-identity.md#id-26-continuous-authentication). |
| SC-24 | Fail in Known State | System-Specific | Planned | The firewalls, the access proxy, the VDI brokers, and the cross domain transfer gateway will fail closed. Each preserves its state so it can recover to a known configuration. The SSP describes it under [DI-3.1](../06-ssp/03-device-and-infrastructure.md#di-31-secure-configurations). |
| SC-28 | Protection of Information at Rest | System-Specific | Planned | Information at rest will be protected in every store. Each data lake zone, database, and storage service is encrypted, and backups and audit logs sit in immutable storage that no account can alter before its retention ends. The SSP describes it under [DA-2.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-24-default-data-at-rest-encryption). |
| SC-28(1) | Protection of Information at Rest \| Cryptographic Protection | System-Specific | Planned | Every store will be encrypted with AES-256 under keys KESTREL controls, as the DMP sets for each label. Each data lake zone uses its own key, personal fields use column encryption, and model artifacts are encrypted in the registry and on serving nodes. Edge models are encrypted under a key rooted in the HSMs. Reports released to partners are wrapped with Purview Information Protection. The SSP describes them under [AI-8.11](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-811-model-artifact-encryption-and-watermarking), [DA-1.6](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-16-data-rights-management-drm), [DA-2.1](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-21-classification-tied-documentfield-level-encryption), [DA-2.4](../06-ssp/07-data.md#da-24-default-data-at-rest-encryption). |
| SC-39 | Process Isolation | System-Specific | Planned | Each process that handles untrusted or sensitive work will run in its own isolated environment. Every pipeline job runs on a fresh runner pod, every training run in its own containers, and every model evaluation in a disposable environment. Each AI agent tool runs in its own Container Instances group with hypervisor isolation. The SSP describes them under [AP-2.21](../06-ssp/05-application.md#ap-221-ephemeralisolated-build-environments), [AI-3.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-31-secure-experimentation-environment), [AI-4.1](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-41-ephemeral-containerized-training-environments), [AI-7.3](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-73-secure-model-evaluation-environment), [AI-8.7](../06-ssp/06-artificial-intelligence.md#ai-87-agentic-tool-callaction-output-validation). |
